sections.h2: Selling a house in Clifton, NJ
sections.html:
No closing can take place in Clifton without a valid dwelling certificate from the Fire Prevention Bureau. On top of that, the city has been revaluing property, which changes assessed values. Those two items shape the timeline more than the listing does.

Clifton is the second-largest city in Passaic County and a bedroom community for New York. A seller usually owns a one- or two-family house or a condo, and the same city paperwork follows the property whether you list it, sell it yourself or accept an investor's offer. The steps below run in the order you will meet them.

About 91,127 people live in Clifton, up from 90,296 in the 2020 count. The owner-occupied rate is 59.6 percent, the median owner-occupied home is valued at $461,900, and median gross rent is $1,711. With roughly four in ten homes not owner-occupied, many sellers here are landlords as well as owner-occupants.

Buyers ask for neighborhoods by name, so use the right one in your listing.

  • Main Mall is the downtown, and Allwood is the other business district, along Route 3.
  • Athenia and Delawanna each have a train station, and Dutch Hill sits near downtown.
  • Botany Village is the northernmost neighborhood, and Lakeview runs along the western edge.
  • Montclair Heights and Rosemawr are among the wealthier residential areas, with Albion Place beside Garret Mountain Reservation.

Route 3, Route 21, Route 19 and U.S. Route 46 cross the city, and the Garden State Parkway runs through it with interchanges 153 through 156. NJ Transit trains stop at Clifton station and Delawanna station on the Main Line toward Hoboken and Suffern. Buses on the 190, 191, 192 and 195 routes go to the Port Authority Bus Terminal, and routes 13, 27 and 72 go to Newark. The mean commute is 28.3 minutes.

A listing that names the elementary school number and the nearest train station answers two of the first questions buyers ask.

sections.h2: How to get the Clifton dwelling certificate
sections.html:
You file a dwelling application with the Fire Prevention Bureau, at 900 Clifton Avenue, after checking with the Building Department that the property has no open permits. The application must be signed by both the seller and the buyer.

  • Call the Building Department at 973-470-5809 to confirm there are no open permits and to learn where to get the application stamped.
  • Bring the stamped application and payment to Clifton Fire Headquarters. An after-hours drop box is available.
  • Inspections are scheduled on Wednesdays from 9 a.m. to noon, and an adult over 18 has to be present with every area of the structure accessible.
  • Call about seven business days after the inspection, since certificates must be picked up in person.

The certificate depends on passing the building, tax and zoning departments, and it expires six months after the fire department inspection. Schedule it once you have a signed contract and a target closing date.

Clifton dwelling certificate fees, per unit
ServiceFee
Sale certificate, standard$125
Rental certificate, standard$75
Expedited, available within 4 to 20 days$200
Expedited, available within 4 business days$300

Fees are charged per dwelling unit, so a two-family house costs double. Pay by personal check, money order, cashier's check, exact-change cash or credit card with a transaction fee, all made out to the City of Clifton. The city takes neither an application without payment nor payment without an application.

sections.h2: Smoke, carbon monoxide and alarm checks
sections.html:
The inspector looks at smoke detectors, carbon monoxide alarms and a label for homes with backup power. Fix these before the appointment, because failing and rescheduling eats into a closing calendar that already hangs on a Wednesday slot.

  • Smoke detectors on every level, except crawl spaces and unfinished attics reached by pull-down stairs.
  • A detector within 10 feet of the outside of each bedroom door on any floor that has bedrooms.
  • All detectors under 10 years old, with 10-year sealed batteries when battery operated, and hardwired systems kept in service.
  • Carbon monoxide alarms within 10 feet of sleeping areas, with more on each additional floor that has sleeping areas.
  • A central station fire alarm tested beforehand, with the test record from a certified company handed over. Inspectors do not test those systems, and a missing report fails the inspection.

One- and two-family homes also need a label within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and meter, warning about secondary power sources such as generators, solar panels or battery storage. The Fire Prevention Bureau supplies and installs that label on inspection day, so owners with solar should expect it.

Clifton has been carrying out a city-wide revaluation, described on the assessor's page and in a city presentation from January 2026. The last revaluation was in 1991, and the average ratio is 31.87. A ratio that low means assessments sit well below market value, so new values are expected to be higher while the tax rate is meant to fall.

The city's explanation is that a revaluation does not raise the total amount collected. School, county and municipal budgets set the levy, and the revaluation only redistributes it by value. Whether your own bill rises or falls depends on whether your house moved more or less than the city average.

The assessed value on old paperwork may not match the new notice. The appeal deadline is April 1, or May 1 in a newly revalued municipality, and an appeal has to prove value with comparable sales. Call the assessing department at 973-470-5838 for your property record.

sections.h2: Tax due dates and relief programs
sections.html:
Taxes are due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, with a ten-day grace period. The tax collector is at 900 Clifton Avenue, first floor, phone 973-470-5830. Online payment is by e-check only, and a lockbox at City Hall takes mailed or dropped-off payments, but no cash. A $35 fee applies to a returned check caused by wrong account numbers.

The assessor's page lists a $250 deduction for qualifying former service members or surviving spouses and a $250 deduction for seniors or disabled persons. The senior deduction requires age 65 or older, ownership and residence in the house, and annual income of $10,000 or less after permitted exclusions. The state's ANCHOR program for homeowners and renters is linked from the tax collector's page. If you receive any of these, tell your closing attorney so the adjustments come out right.

sections.h2: Where a Clifton deed is recorded
sections.html:
Deeds go to the Passaic County Clerk's Registry Division, 401 Grand Street, Room 113, in Paterson, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. The office does not do title searches or record surveys. Recording rules to plan around:

  • Deeds must carry the words Prepared by, the tax block, lot and consideration.
  • Every document needs a record and return address, and original signatures with names printed beneath.
  • Use the official county cover sheet, or pay an extra $20 per document.
  • Pay the realty transfer fee with an attorney trust check, title agency trust check, certified check or cash.

The county posts the seller forms you need: the Affidavit of Consideration for Use by Seller, the Seller Residency Certification, the Nonresident Seller Tax Declaration and the waiver form. An owner who has moved out of New Jersey is treated as a nonresident for the sale, which can mean an estimated payment at closing. A federal principal residence exclusion may shelter up to $250,000 of gain, or $500,000 for a qualifying couple.

faqs.q: Can I close on a Clifton house without a dwelling certificate?
faqs.a: No. The city's instructions state that no closing shall take place without a valid Certificate of Inspection, and the certificate expires six months after the fire department inspection.

faqs.q: How much does a Clifton sale certificate cost?
faqs.a: The standard fee is $125 per unit for a sale. Expedited service costs $200 per unit for a 4 to 20 day turnaround or $300 per unit for four business days.

faqs.q: When does the Clifton fire department inspect?
faqs.a: Inspections run on Wednesdays between 9 a.m. and noon, and an adult over 18 must be home. Call about seven business days afterward, because certificates are picked up in person.

faqs.q: When are Clifton property taxes due?
faqs.a: February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, with a ten-day grace period. Online payment is by e-check only.

faqs.q: When must I appeal a Clifton assessment?
faqs.a: The deadline is April 1, or May 1 in a municipality that has just been revalued. An appeal has to prove value with comparable sales.
